chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd ibn Tareyf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then as for him who gives and is pious and believes in that which is best [reward], Allah the Exalted will give for one [good deed] tenfold or up to a hundred thousand; so what is more We will facilitate for him the easy [end].' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not desire any good except that Allah makes it easy for him.'

And as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient, [the Imam] said: 'He is stingy with what Allah gave him and rejects the best [reward], believing that Allah gives tenfold or up to a hundred thousand for one [good deed]; so what is more We will facilitate for him the difficult [end].' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not desire any evil except that Allah makes it easy for him.'
And his wealth will not avail him when he falls.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, he does not fall into a well, nor from a mountain, nor from a wall, but he falls into the Fire of Hell.'
ai.seo_question: How does the Imam interpret the 'fall' of the stingy man in Surah Al-Layl?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) elucidates Surah Al-Layl by contrasting the generous believer, for whom Allah facilitates ease and multiplies rewards, with the stingy disbeliever, for whom evil is made easy. He specifically interprets the phrase 'wa ma yughnee 'anhu maluhu idha taradda' to mean that the wealthy man's fall is not physical but a descent into the Fire of Hell, emphasizing the spiritual consequence of hoarding wealth over divine trust.
